# save_game_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Archive, restore and back up game saves.

## Synopsis

```
save_game_tool [options]
```

## Description

Works on each selected game that has a JSON entry. Two directories are involved: the
live save directory in the cache (`Wine` or `Sandboxie` below it for `Computer` games,
depending on the host), and the save archive directory in the local locker,
`Gaming/Saves/<category>/<subcategory>/<game>`.

Actions:

- `Pack`: zip the live save directory, test the zip, and skip it if an identical
  archive is already in the save archive directory. Otherwise copy it to that path,
  as `<game>_<timestamp>.zip`, in each locker selected by `-l`.
- `Unpack`: extract the newest archive from the save archive directory into the live
  save directory.
- `Export`: for store games, copy the save files from the store's save paths on this
  machine (as recorded in the game's JSON entry) into a temporary tree and pack that.
  For other games, the same as `Pack`.
- `Import`: for non-store games, the same as `Unpack` when there is an archive to
  unpack. For store games, nothing.
- `ImportSavePaths`: for store games, list the files inside the save archives,
  convert them to tokenized store paths, and merge them into the game's JSON entry.

Games are selected with `-c`, `-s` and `-n`; any that is omitted matches everything,
so with none of them the action runs over every game.

## Options

### Action

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Not used by any action. |
| `-a, --action <action>` | What to do with each selected game's saves; see the list above. Default: `Pack`. Allowed: `Pack`, `Unpack`, `Import`, `Export`, `ImportSavePaths`. |

### Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Locker to copy new archives to for `Pack` and `Export`; `All` means every configured locker. Default: `All`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Capture the current saves of an installed Steam game

```bash
save_game_tool -a Export -c Computer -s Steam -n "Hades (World)" -l Local
```

### Preview exporting every store game's saves

```bash
save_game_tool -a Export -c Computer -p -v
```

### Pack a Switch game's saves into every configured locker

```bash
save_game_tool -a Pack -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -n "Game Name"
```

### Restore the newest save archive into place

```bash
save_game_tool -a Unpack -c Computer -s Steam -n "Hades (World)"
```

### Record save paths for all Steam games from their archives

```bash
save_game_tool -a ImportSavePaths -c Computer -s Steam
```

## Notes

- `Pack` archives what is already in the live save directory; to capture fresh saves from an installed store game use `Export`.
- Every pack or export writes a new timestamped archive rather than replacing an old one, unless an identical archive already exists.
- Archives are copied to the lockers as plain zip files, without encryption.
- The first game that fails stops the run.
